newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says plan to prevent further crises.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says plan to prevent further crises.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said the National Program to Finance Development (Pronafide) promises healthy finances and will prevent financial crises through 2000.
Ortiz discussed the three-year development plan in a private television interview late Saturday, state news agency Notimex said.
The program was announced last week and aims for gross domestic product (GDP) growth of about five percent per year and higher domestic savings levels.
Ortiz said the government commits in the plan to prevent a financial crisis at the end of President Ernesto Zedillo's administration, Notimex said.

In 1994, the final year of former president Carlos Salinas de Gortari's six-year term, an overvalued peso led to a sharp devaluation in the currency that plunged the economy into its worst recession in six decades.
Although the peso's value is no longer at a fixed exchange rate, many Mexicans fear that politicians will let the peso overvalue for election reasons and force further slides in the currency.
Ortiz also said that the country's foreign debt is no longer a risk, referring to 1995 debt levels, Notimex said.
